member.name: T:UnderAutomation.Yaskawa.Common.IDhParameters
member.summary: Denavit-Hartenberg parameters of a 6-axis Yaskawa arm (axes S, L, U, R, B, T).
member.remarks:
Parameters use the modified DH convention (Craig): T(i) = Rx(alpha(i-1)) * Tx(a(i-1)) * Rz(theta(i) + q(i)) * Tz(d(i)). Only the values that change from one robot to another are stored. The full table is:
alpha = (0, -90, 0, -90, 90, -90) a = (0, A1, A2, A3, 0, 0) theta = (0, Theta2, Theta3, 0, Theta5, Theta6) d = (0, 0, 0, D4, D5, D6)
Theta6 is 0 for robots and 180 for robots. The robot frame origin is on the S axis, at the height of the L axis.

member.name: T:UnderAutomation.Yaskawa.YaskawaRobot
member.summary: Main entry point for communicating with Yaskawa Motoman robots. This class provides methods to connect, monitor, and control the robot through multiple interfaces: High Speed Ethernet Server, Ethernet Server (Host Control over TCP), HTTP and FTP.

remarks.para: The YaskawaRobot class encapsulates all communication functionality with Yaskawa Motoman robot controllers that support the High Speed Ethernet Server protocol and/or Host Control function. This includes the YRC1000 (micro), MOTOMAN NEXT, DX100 / DX200, FS100, ERC / XRC / MRC controllers.

Before using this class, ensure that:
The robot controller has the required communication function enabled
Network connectivity is established between your application and the robot
Appropriate safety measures are in place when controlling robot motion
